TIR satellite nadir observations can provide information on the chemical and microphysics properties of UTLS sulfate aerosols.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sensitivity of thermal infra-red satellite nadir instruments, like IASI and MODIS, to the chemical composition of UTLS sulfate aerosols is limited.
the sensitivity to UTLS sulfate aerosols, in terms of degrees of freedom for signal and retrieval uncertainties, is higher for the high spectral resolution IASI-like approach.
TIR nadir observations, in the spectral range between 700 and 1200 cm-1, are sensitive to UTLS secondary sulfate particles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TIR spectral signature of UTLS sulfate aerosols can be exploited to retrieve their chemical and microphysics properties from nadir satellite observations.

, despite the large uncertainties affecting the retrieval of UTLS aerosol parameters from TIR satellite observations, the information content of these measurements is large enough to allow for the retrieval of the aerosol extinction properties, at least for a limited set of aerosol parameters, with reasonable uncertainties.
